environment.description: Same EKS cluster but the pod runs in namespace 'monitoring-restricted'. A Cilium CiliumNetworkPolicy (not native Kubernetes NetworkPolicy) with entity-based selectors is applied. The policy uses 'toEntities' with a deny rule, but Cilium's entity resolution for link-local addresses depends on the 'enable-remote-node-identity' helm value being set to true (which it is in this cluster's values.yaml but not visible in the policy manifest itself). Additionally, a secondary native K8s NetworkPolicy exists that allows egress only to kube-dns on port 53/UDP and to the API server CIDR 10.0.0.0/16, but this policy alone would not block metadata access since 169.254.169.254 could be argued to fall outside its explicit allow list only if the CNI correctly interprets the implicit deny semantics (which varies by CNI implementation). The cluster also runs kube-proxy in iptables mode with a custom iptables rule on nodes dropping packets to 169.254.169.254 from pod CIDRs, managed via a DaemonSet running in kube-system.
